title: The Past Continuous
subtitle: What were you doing at six o'clock yesterday?

beats.caption: I <v>was walking</v> through the grass when I <v>saw</v> three sheep!
What <v>were</v> you <v>doing</v> at six o'clock yesterday?

say: Was walking. Were doing. Mia is talking about an action that was in progress in the past. This is the past continuous.
In this lesson you'll learn when to use it, how to make it, and how to use it together with the past simple. Let's go.

data.heading: When do we use the past continuous?
points: An action in progress at a moment in the past
Two actions happening at the same time

say: We use the past continuous for an action that was in progress at a moment in the past. At six o'clock yesterday, Mia was walking. She started before six, and she continued after six.
We also use it for the background of a story: the sun was shining, the birds were singing.
And for two long actions at the same time: Mia was walking, and the sheep were eating.
The form is simple: was or were, plus the verb with i n g.
I, he, she and it take was. I was walking.
You, we and they take were. They were eating.
Mia was smiling.
The sheep were sleeping.
Most verbs just add i n g: walk, walking.
If the verb ends in e, drop the e: make, making.
Short verbs that end consonant, vowel, consonant double the last letter: run, running. Sit, sitting.
Verbs that end in i e change it to y: lie, lying. Die, dying.
And verbs ending in y keep the y: study, studying. Play, playing.
Look at Mia. At six o'clock yesterday, she was walking through the grass. The sun was going down, and the sheep were eating quietly.
beats.caption: At six o'clock, Mia <v>was walking</v>. The sheep <v>were eating</v>.

say: The past continuous often works together with the past simple. The past continuous is the long action. The past simple is the short action that interrupts it.
I was walking, when I saw the sheep.
She was reading, when the phone rang.
While usually goes with the long action: while I was walking, the birds were singing.
While we were eating, it started to rain.

data.heading: Negative sentences
data.note: wasn't = was not · weren't = were not

say: For negatives, use wasn't or weren't, plus i n g.
I wasn't sleeping.
She wasn't listening.
We weren't playing.
They weren't working.
Wasn't means was not, and weren't means were not.

beats.caption: I <v>wasn't sleeping</v>. I <v>was watching</v> the sunset!

say: For questions, put was or were before the subject.
Were you sleeping? No, I wasn't.
Was Mia walking home? Yes, she was.
What were you doing? I was watching TV.
Where was she going? She was going home.
Some verbs describe states, not actions. We don't usually use them with i n g.
Know: I knew the answer, not I was knowing.
Want: she wanted a cat.
Like: we liked the film.
Believe: he believed her.
Now some common mistakes.
I was walk to school. We need i n g: I was walking to school.
I walking yesterday. We need was: I was walking yesterday.
While I saw the sheep. Saw is a short action, so use when: when I saw the sheep.
They was playing. They takes were: they were playing.

data.heading: Mia's evening
data.sub: Notice the long and the short actions

say: Now listen to Mia's evening, and notice the long actions and the short actions.
Yesterday evening, Mia was walking through the field. The sun was shining and the sheep were eating. Suddenly, she stopped and counted them.
beats.caption: Mia <v>was walking</v>. The sheep <v>were eating</v>. She <v>stopped</v>.
<v>While</v> I <v>was walking</v> home, the stars <v>were coming</v> out.

beats.say_answer: Was watching. An action in progress at eight p m.

data.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
I was walking home ___ I saw Mia.

beats.say_answer: When. Saw is the short action.
Knew. Know is a state verb, no i n g.
Were. Were you sleeping at midnight?

data.heading: Remember
items: Action in progress at a past moment

say: Let's remember. The past continuous is for an action in progress at a moment in the past, made with was or were plus i n g.
Use it for the long action, and the past simple for the short action that interrupts it.
Don't use it with state verbs like know, want and like.
